text: Looking at it now: the likely cause is that in errors.go `Unwrap()` is defined on `*Error` while `Error()` is on the value `Error`, so a gin.Error *value* inside a `fmt.Errorf("%w", ...)` chain doesn't satisfy `interface{ Unwrap() error }` and errors.Is/errors.As can't traverse into it. I'm verifying and fixing (value receiver), then running the full test suite to make sure nothing regresses. ETA ~10 min.

Fixed. Cause: in errors.go, `Unwrap()` had a pointer receiver while `Error()` has a value receiver, so a gin.Error *value* inside a `fmt.Errorf("%w", ...)` chain didn't implement `interface{ Unwrap() error }` and errors.Is/errors.As couldn't traverse into it (the pointer form worked, which is why you saw the asymmetry).

Change (errors.go, one line): `func (msg *Error) Unwrap() error` → `func (msg Error) Unwrap() error`. `*Error` still has Unwrap in its method set, so the pointer form is unaffected.

Verified with your exact snippet (both value and pointer forms now return true for errors.Is and errors.As, plus errors.Unwrap and multi-layer wrapping), and `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` and `go test -race ./...` all pass with no pre-existing test regressing.

On it. Likely cause: in response_writer.go `WriteHeader` unconditionally sets `w.status = code`, even after the response has already been written (whereas `WriteHeaderNow`/`Write` ignore later status changes), so `Status()` reports a status that was never sent. I'm confirming against the in-repo docs/tests, applying the minimal fix, and running the full suite. ETA ~10 min.

Fixed. Cause: `responseWriter.WriteHeader` set `w.status = code` unconditionally, even after the response was already flushed — while `WriteHeaderNow`/`Write`/`Flush` all guard on `!w.Written()`. So the status on the wire stayed 200 but `Status()` tracked the late 401. (The code even printed the "[WARNING] Headers were already written. Wanted to override status code 200 with 401" message and then overrode anyway, contradicting the README's documented behavior.)

Change (response_writer.go, one line): in `WriteHeader`, `return` right after the warning when `w.Written()` is true, so the status is only set before the header is flushed.

Verified: your sequence now gives `Status() == 200` (client 200), normal `WriteHeader(401)` still gives 401, the documented warning is still emitted, and `gofmt`/`go build`/`go vet`/`go test ./...`/`go test -race ./...` all pass with no pre-existing test regressing.

On it. Likely cause: tree.go keeps a per-method skip cache of paths that didn't match (the `skips`/`tskips` structure used by `getValue`); when you add a route later with `addRoute`, that cache isn't invalidated, so the previously-missed path short-circuits and the handler runs with empty Params. I'm confirming, applying the minimal fix (invalidate/clear the cache on route addition), and running the full suite plus a repro. ETA ~12 min.

On it. That panic is in the case-insensitive path search in tree.go (reached via RedirectFixedPath): with a static route and a param route under the same prefix, the search hits a node type it doesn't handle and panics instead of returning the fixed path or not-found. I'm reproducing it, fixing the unhandled case minimally, and checking that case-insensitive/trailing-slash redirects still work. ETA ~12 min.

On it. That's an out-of-range slice in context.go's `NegotiateFormat`: the accepted value is compared/sliced using the length of the offered format without checking the accepted string is at least that long, so `image/tiff-fx` vs `image/tiff` panics. I'm reproducing it, applying the minimal bounds/matching fix, and verifying the documented matching behavior (exact, `;`-params, `*/*`, multi-offer) still holds. ETA ~12 min.

On it. `FileAttachment` builds `Content-Disposition` by interpolating the filename directly, so embedded `"` and `\` break out of the quoted parameter (header injection). I'm fixing it to escape those characters while keeping ordinary filenames byte-identical, and running the full suite. ETA ~12 min.

Fixed. Cause: `Context.FileAttachment` built the header by raw concatenation — `attachment; filename="`+filename+`"` — without escaping `"` or `\`, so a filename like `evil"; dummy="x.sh` injected a second parameter. (The non-ASCII branch was already safe since it uses `url.QueryEscape`.)

Change: added a small `escapeQuotes` helper in utils.go (backslash-escapes `\` and `"`) and used it in FileAttachment's Content-Disposition. Ordinary filenames are byte-identical (`attachment; filename="report.pdf"`); the malicious one now yields `attachment; filename="evil\"; dummy=\"x.sh"`, which parses back to exactly one filename parameter. `gofmt`/`go build`/`go vet`/`go test ./...`/`go test -race ./...` all pass, no pre-existing test regressed.

Fixed. Cause (slightly different from my first guess): the engine caches contexts in a sync.Pool, and each context preallocates its `params`/`skippedNodes` scratch slices sized by `maxParams`/`maxSections` at allocation time. `addRoute` grew those maxima but never invalidated the pooled contexts, so a context allocated during the earlier 404 was reused with too-small slices — `getValue` then silently dropped the params (200 with empty Params) or panicked on the catch-all/skippedNodes paths.

Change (gin.go only): added `Engine.resetPool()`, which replaces the pool with one whose `New` allocates a fresh context, and call it in `addRoute` right after `maxParams`/`maxSections` are updated. No new locking.

Verified with a standalone repro: route added after a 404 now returns 200 with `name="john"`, `last_name="smith"`, `wild="/is/super/great"` — identical to registering the route up front — plus static/param/sibling/wildcard cases and a live httptest server. `gofmt`/`go build`/`go vet`/`go test ./...`/`go test -race ./...` all pass; no pre-existing test regressed.
